newsitem.title: USA: TransTexas to boost South Texas drilling.
newsitem.headline: TransTexas to boost South Texas drilling.

text.p: TransTexas Gas Corp said Tuesday directors approved a significant expansion of its development drilling activity in the Bob West North natural gas field in Zapata County, South Texas.
The company said that it would immediately increase rig activity in the 15,900 acre area to six rigs from the current level of two.
TransTexas said it believes Bob West North will ultimately prove to contain recoverable reserves as great as the company's present Lobo Trend proved reserves, some 700 billion cubic feet equivalent.
The company said the goal of the increased drilling is an additional 20 wells in the field by the end of its fiscal year, January 31.

Recent production and reserve additions from this block have been sufficiently attractive to justify re-focusing the company's development expenditures upon Bob West North, which is expected to result in capital expenditures of $40 million for the 20 wells, TransTexas said.
Spokesman Simon Ward said this spending does not represent an increase in total capital spending, but a refocusing of planned outlays.

Since the beginning of the company's fiscal year, on Feb. 1, five wells drilled in the area added over 210 million cubic feet of natural gas per day in production and are estimated to have added 70 billion cubic feet of natural gas equivalent in proved reserves, which totaled 129.3 billion cubic feet on February 1.

TransTexas said it is in the process of acquiring pipeline right-of-way for construction of 21 miles of 30-inch line to connect from the Occidental Petroleum Corp's MidCon Texas 24-inch joint venture pipeline in the Fandango area to its Thompsonville, Texas, 30-inch pipeline.

This will allow delivery of high Btu natural gas from Bob West North, directly through the TransTexas pipeline, to its Agua Dulce marketing hub and increase transportation capacity from Bob West North to 600 million cubic feet per day, the company said.

In addition to the focus upon Bob West North, ongoing development of the Lobo Trend will continue with 3-5 rigs. The company said it is planning to build a 30-inch pipeline from Exxon Corp's King Ranch NGL processing plant to TransTexas' Agua Dulce marketing hub. This addition will expand TransTexas' capacity to transport company and third-party production and market natural gas to the major consuming areas east of the Rocky Mountains to 1.2 billion cubic feet per day. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
